algorithm.byte_order: big-endian for every multi-byte integer (network byte order)
algorithm.layout: message_id:16 || sent_at_ms:u64be || source_endpoint_len:u8 || source_endpoint || destination_endpoint_len:u8 || destination_endpoint || media_type_len:u8 || media_type || payload_len:u32be || payload
notes: message_id is exactly 16 bytes — 128 bits — never a printable form.
source_endpoint_len is 52: a source is always present, a derived EndpointId (ENDPOINTS.md §EndpointId), taken from the sender's lease and never caller-chosen.
destination_endpoint_len is 52, or 0 for the receiver's configured default endpoint: not an empty name and not fan-out. Any other endpoint length is malformed.
media_type_len = 0 encodes ABSENCE; no empty media-type string exists on the wire.
payload_len is u32be and precedes the payload even when the payload is empty.
sent_at_ms is diagnostic: not authorization, ordering, freshness, replay-window, or dedup input.
algorithm.test_keys: Every endpoint id here is a TEST-ONLY derived id: the Ed25519 key whose seed is SHA-256('interweave/test-only/endpoint-key/v1' || 0x00 || name), name in <field>_test_key (tests/support endpoint_keys::endpoint_id). Public by construction; never an identity outside a test.

$comment: Vectors are DERIVED from the layout decided in DIRECT.md — no ADR publishes a golden frame, so this file is anchored by its `adr` list rather than by a per-vector `frozen_by`. Byte order was unspecified until this fixture forced the question; DIRECT.md now pins big-endian, matching the IPC length prefix and the content fingerprint. There is deliberately NO `contract` URN here: DIRECT.md and the direct family manifest both record that the request frame is a byte layout JSON Schema cannot express, so a schema pointer would name a contract this file does not verify. The previous pointer named the dedup-key schema, which is a different concept entirely.

vectors.name: explicit-destination
vectors.description: The ordinary case: both endpoints present, a short text payload.

vectors.name: default-destination
vectors.description: destination_endpoint_len = 0 asks for the receiver's configured default endpoint. It is NOT an empty endpoint name, and never means fan-out.

vectors.name: absent-media-type
vectors.description: media_type_len = 0 encodes ABSENCE. No empty media-type string exists on the wire, and this maps to media_present=0 in the content fingerprint.

vectors.name: empty-payload
vectors.description: payload_len = 0 with the u32be length still present. An empty payload is legal; an empty media type is not.

vectors.name: two-other-test-keys
vectors.description: Both endpoint fields at their one legal length, 52, from two keys no other vector uses. On 3.0.0 there is no ceiling vector: an endpoint field has no other legal length, so this replaces the former 64-byte label case.

vectors.name: sent-at-ms-is-not-fingerprinted
vectors.description: Identical to explicit-destination except for sent_at_ms. The FRAME bytes differ; the content fingerprint does not — sent_at_ms is diagnostic only and excluded from dedup identity.
